proposed.citation: Elisabeth Gassiat, Alice Cleynen, and Stéphane Robin (2016), ``Inference in Finite State Space Non Parametric Hidden Markov Models and Applications,'' Statistics and Computing 26, 61--71, especially Theorem 1.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Adds the theorem-level restricted-HMM comparator required by the ExactID reclassification.

proposed.citation: Elizabeth S. Allman, Catherine Matias, and John A. Rhodes (2009), ``Identifiability of Parameters in Latent Structure Models with Many Observed Variables,'' Annals of Statistics 37, 3099--3132, especially Theorem 6.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Adds the generic finite-HMM theorem required for a precise nonnested comparison.

proposed.comparator_claim: Under RSM, first-order M, and ID, Proposition 14 identifies the full finite-mixture parameter \(\psi\) when \(T_0\geq k+1\), \(T\geq2(k+1)\), and \(J\leq|\mathcal X|^k\); Proposition 15 adds TI-LT for latent-type ATT.
proposed.matched_by: The present theorem permits the common absorbing row excluded by ID(b), uses fixed known \(J\leq m\) and \(2m-1\) selected active anchor-star rank conditions, and identifies active targets on the broad face with full targets only on the no-date-\(1\)-absorption subface.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 reconstructs Markov-mixture primitives under its time-homogeneous and component-rank conditions.
proposed.matched_by: The present known-\(J\) construction uses selected active minors and stochastic normalization without time homogeneity and does not claim to subsume the interior reconstruction theorem.

proposed.comparator_claim: The paper reconstructs homogeneous Markov mixtures under its state-count and nondegeneracy restrictions.
proposed.matched_by: The present result is causal and time-varying, permits a shared absorbing boundary, and fixes known \(J\) no larger than the active-state count.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 identifies a nonparametric HMM from three observations when the hidden-state count is known, emission laws are linearly independent, and the hidden transition matrix has full rank.
proposed.matched_by: That HMM has an evolving hidden state and conditionally independent emissions; the present nonnested model has a time-invariant type, an observed Markov state, time-varying kernels, and a shared singular absorbing row.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 6 gives generic finite-HMM parameter identification from \(2k+1\) observations under its binomial hidden-state/emission-size condition.
proposed.matched_by: The present theorem is a pointwise active-sublaw and causal-ATT construction with a sharp initial-absorber frontier, not a generic full-HMM parameter-identification result.

proposed.comparator_claim: The paper develops aggregate duration difference-in-differences under absorption-oriented restrictions.
proposed.matched_by: The present theorem reconstructs latent-type multistate contributions and isolates the initial-absorber frontier for conditional effects.

proposed.comparator_claim: The paper estimates latent conditional moments by simultaneous diagonalization and derives regular asymptotics for estimated spectral weights.
proposed.matched_by: It is precedent for differentiating spectral estimators; the present analytic map additionally contains absorbing-boundary row sums, a full-row-rank pseudoinverse, and full-predecessor-row transport.

proposed.comparator_claim: The paper develops Gaussian approximation and multiplier bootstrap methods for maxima of sums.
proposed.matched_by: The present fixed-dimensional proof integrates an exact conditional Gaussian multiplier with the buffered empirical guard and analytic recovery remainder.

proposed.comparator_claim: The paper gives Gaussian comparison and anti-concentration bounds allowing arbitrary dependence with positive coordinate variances.
proposed.matched_by: The present fixed-\(q\) singular-correlation quantile-continuity step is self-contained and is combined with uniform guard acceptance and covariance consistency.

proposed.comparator_claim: The paper supplies a general semiparametric tangent-space framework for efficiency bounds.
proposed.matched_by: It motivates the open restricted-model question only; this paper constructs no restricted observed-law score chart and claims only saturated finite-multinomial efficiency.

proposed.comparator_claim: The paper analyzes weak, semi-strong, and strong identification asymptotic regimes.
proposed.matched_by: Those weak-identification regimes are excluded by the fixed \(\kappa\)-buffer and are not invoked in the regular guarded-band theorem.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Replaces generic positioning by the ExactID theorem-level Ahn--Kasahara delta, names both HMM comparators, states the anchor-star versus all-slice distinction, and limits inference comparisons to their actual roles.
